channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Altered Cognitive Control and Cortical Oscillatory Dynamics in Athletes With ACL Reconstruction During Decision-Making Under Uncertainty.
item.description: In 90 open-skill athletes (45 non-ACLR, 45 ACLR), ACLR athletes showed slower response times and lower accuracy (d = 0.75-1.09) during a probabilistic go/no-go task, with attenuated midfrontal theta power prestimulus and elevated power during the target phase, reflecting a shift to reactive cognitive control, impaired motor cortical disinhibition, and less efficient visual-attentional resource deployment.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Diagnosis, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport after Athletic Hamstring Injury: An ICCUS Society Consensus Statement.
item.description: An ICCUS Society modified Delphi consensus (n=17 experts) for athletic hamstring injuries (AHSI) achieved consensus on 54 statements (mean agreement 89.88%), supporting standardized terminology, MRI/ultrasound for diagnosis, individualized and criterion-based rehabilitation, progressive tissue loading, early neuromuscular control, gradual running/agility progression, pain-free sprinting, objective strength assessment, sport-specific workloads, and athlete readiness as key RTS criteria.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative study of therapeutic ultrasound and whole-body vibration as adjuncts to passive stretching on knee joint range of motion and functional ability in children with hemiplegic cerebral palsy: a randomized trial
item.description: A randomized trial (n=60 children aged 4-6 years with hemiplegic cerebral palsy) compared therapeutic ultrasound (US) and whole-body vibration (WBV) as adjuncts to passive stretching. The WBV group showed significantly greater improvements in active knee extension ROM (13.82% vs 7.05%) and GMFM scores (22.72% vs 11.32%) over 12 weeks (p<0.01).
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Effects of Exercise Type and Duration on Pain, Function, and Quality of Life in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review With Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A Bayesian network meta-analysis of 35 trials (n=3808) found short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had the largest effect for pain (SMD = -0.937), function (SMD = -0.590), and QoL (SMD = 0.663) in patients with knee osteoarthritis.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of short-foot and toe-curl exercises on movement control during single-leg landing after ACL reconstruction: An exploratory randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A multicenter exploratory RCT (N=38) found that short-foot exercise (SFE) led to earlier improvements in hip adduction excursion during single-leg landing compared to toe-curl exercise (TCE) in ACLR patients, with between-group difference of -6.30° (95% CI, -9.19 to -3.41; ES, -1.41) at 6 weeks.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise-based rehabilitation interventions for kinesiophobia after total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
item.description: A systematic review of 11 RCTs (N=1,096) found that exercise-based rehabilitation was associated with a reduction in kinesiophobia (SMD = -1.22, 95% CI [-1.72, -0.72]) and improvements in knee function (SMD = 1.19, 95% CI [0.67, 1.71]) after total knee arthroplasty, although the certainty of evidence was low for both outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Robotic Assessment of Thumb Proprioception after Stroke: Reliability, Validity, and Sensitivity.
item.description: A novel robotic assessment (SCJ) for thumb proprioception in chronic stroke survivors demonstrated good reliability, validity, and sensitivity, identifying deficits in 61% of participants, significantly more than the FMA-S.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Neurocognitive Factors in ACL Injury: The Missing Piece in Rehabilitation and Prevention? A Scoping Review.
item.description: A scoping review of 42 studies identified dual-task interference and visual attention as the most investigated neurocognitive domains in ACL injury. Neurocognitive training interventions show potential benefits in visuomotor efficiency, movement compliance, and return to sport readiness, suggesting neurocognitive factors are a missing component in current ACL rehabilitation and prevention frameworks.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Predictive value of handgrip strength, calf circumference, and the SARC-F questionnaire for institutionalization and mortality after hip fracture – a real-world cohort study
item.description: A real-world cohort study of 222 older adults found that a positive SARC-F questionnaire screen strongly predicted institutionalization (OR 8.20, 95% CI 2.34–28.7) and mortality (HR 3.00, 95% CI 1.11–8.07) one year after hip fracture, while handgrip strength and calf circumference did not show consistent association.
item.author: Aging Clin Exp Res

item.title: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial
item.description: The PROSpect trial found no evidence that prone positioning or HFOV improve ventilator-free days in early, moderate-to-severe PARDS, recommending against their routine use as first-line strategies.
item.author: The Lancet

item.title: Adherence System Usability Patient Experience and Psychosocial Impact in Robot Assisted Gait Neurorehabilitation A Cross Sectional Study.
item.description: In a single-center observational study of 250 adults with neurological conditions, greater adherence (mean participation 86.35%), system usability (mean SUS 72.79), and neurorehabilitation experience (mean NREQ 27.84) were associated with a favorable psychosocial impact (mean PIADS 1.67), with adherence correlating with SUS (r s = 0.41), NREQ (r s = 0.49), and PIADS (r s = 0.53; all p < 0.001).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Gamified Versus Traditional Balance Training: Effects on Balance and Motivation in Collegiate Student-Athletes.
item.description: A quasi-experimental trial (n=30) found gamified (Wii Fit) and traditional (wobble board) balance training similarly improved mSEBT composite scores (gamified: +21.6 ± 11.9 cm, d = 1.84; traditional: +18.5 ± 14.6 cm, d = 1.54) compared to control (p < 0.01). Gamified training resulted in higher intrinsic motivation (5.0 ± 1.2 vs. 3.2 ± 1.3; p < 0.01, d = 1.50).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Effects of Neurostimulation- and Technology-Augmented Robot-Assisted Training on Upper-Limb Motor Recovery After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis
item.description: This systematic review and network meta-analysis aimed to compare robot-assisted training alone with neurostimulation- or technology-augmented RAT for poststroke upper-limb recovery.
item.author: Archives of PM&R

item.title: What are the barriers and facilitators to engagement with physiotherapy among women experiencing adverse effects associated with menopause?
item.description: A qualitative study (n=12) identified fatigue, cognitive issues, low self-efficacy, and negative language as barriers to physiotherapy engagement for women with menopause-related MSK pain, while direct inquiry about menopause and feeling listened to were facilitators.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Investigating the Feasibility of Locomotor Training for Children Under 5 Years With Complex Neurodisabilties.
item.description: A single-group pre-post study (n=71, mean age 2.8 years) found a 6-week locomotor training program feasible and beneficial for young children with neurodisabilities, showing improvements in Goal Attainment Scaling (12.8 to 56.2) and other mobility outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Remote Ischemic Conditioning Modulates Spinal Reflex Excitability in Healthy Young Adults: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial
item.description: A pilot RCT found that remote ischemic conditioning (RIC) paired with balance training reduced the Hslp/Mslp ratio (p=0.02) and improved balance performance (p=0.02) more than sham in healthy young adults, suggesting RIC may augment neuroplastic adaptations.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Early postoperative functional exercise adherence and its association with 3-month hip functional recovery among older adults after femoral neck fracture surgery: a prospective observational study.
item.description: A prospective observational study (n=230) found that before-discharge functional exercise adherence was moderate in older adults after femoral neck fracture surgery and was positively associated with 3-month hip functional recovery (r=0.838, p<0.001). Adherence was linked to kinesiophobia (r=-0.753), pain (r=-0.399), self-efficacy (r=0.754), and social support (r=0.893).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical exercise therapy for autism spectrum disorder: a scoping review of systematic reviews
item.description: A scoping review of 50 systematic reviews (published 2013-2025) on physical exercise therapy (PET) for individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) found that PET may improve motor, social, behavioral, and sleep outcomes. However, the findings are limited by low methodological quality, high heterogeneity, and lack of long-term follow-up.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of Plyometric Exercises Versus Flatfoot Corrective Exercises on Balance and Foot Posture in Obese Children with a Flexible Flatfoot: A Comparative Study
item.description: An 8-week comparative study in 120 obese children with flexible flatfoot found that both plyometric and flatfoot corrective exercises improved foot posture and balance; however, plyometric training showed greater gains in balance (median path length: 30.39 cm vs. 37.45 cm, p < 0.001) and slightly better foot posture improvements for the left foot (p = 0.028).
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: A Retrospective Real-World Assessment of Motor Status After Stroke Using a Home-Based Brain-Computer Interface
item.description: A retrospective observational study of 452 stroke survivors using at-home BCI therapy found mean UEFM scores improved by 4.3 points at 12 weeks, reached the MCID (5.25 points) by 16 weeks, and continued to increase to 8.1 points at 52 weeks, especially in patients with severe chronic impairment.
item.author: medRxiv
